An uncluttered default: 'Clean' in v2 and 'Simple View' in the early engine are both defaults. Details live in tooltips and optional panels.
Modes Scalping, Day Trading (the default, D/4H/1H), Swing and Custom; Auto from the chart timeframe in the early engine.
Instruments: Gold futures 5m (screenshot), MNQ/MES/NQ/ES on 1m/5m, XAUUSD.

Plain trader wording: Target, PoT, BSL/SSL, BUY-SIDE/SELL-SIDE, BULLISH/BEARISH, short codes (BEFVG, BUOB, PDH). The user writes informally, is a trader rather than a programmer, wants short plain replies, and wants the final script pasted in one code block plus the file.

From the early engine: BUY/SELL with entry, stop and target; $-risk sizing; a daily loss limit; one trade at a time; NY core hours. Blue/red reserved for trades and a magenta DOL, which conflicts with the later neon green/red choice.
Strong emphasis on non-repainting in every product, and on honesty: the READMEs report losing results plainly and say 'not a probability' and 'not a guarantee'.

Conflicts for the architect: the 'PoT: 70.1%' label vs spec 4.7/15 (show it as a probability only once the per-chart scorecard passes); the spec's default BUY/SELL markers and green/red path vs the reference, which has neither (they can coexist); LFP's directional % and large fills vs spec 17; the early engine's NQ-specific costs and hours vs spec 2.1.
lessonsFromTesting: Early-engine PoT research (README claim; scripts absent; 26 datasets: 13 markets x 5m/1h, about 1.1M bars, about 519k resolved targets, 70/30 time split). Brier skill: analytic about 0.14, empirical+analytic 0.192, v5 bins 0.194, v6 learning 0.201, all 20 ICT features 0.192 (over-fits). Supported: distance and the volatility regime drive touch probability.

Early-engine rejections (README claim): liquidity type (EQH/EQL, sessions, PDH/PDL, HTF levels), HTF bias, sweeps, premium/discount, confluence and the DOL score had no out-of-sample value. The DOL side was taken first 59.3% of the time, equal to distance alone (59.3%). HTF-aligned break setups won 48.7% with the signal vs 49.8% against it (1-ATR symmetric).

Sweep Reversal (README claim; MNQ/NQ and S&P 1m/5m; 4 weeks 1m + 10 weeks 5m CME + 6 weeks 1m index, Mar-Apr 2025): 1,350 trades, 38% win, -0.06R per trade. With the order-flow filter: 357 trades, 49% win, +0.09R, positive only in Mar-Apr 2025 and negative on recent CME data, so not proven. DOL Direction with order flow: 1,235 trades, 53% win, -0.02R per trade.

Order-flow proxy (README claim; 19 days 1m + 49 days 5m CME + 42 days 1m index): a 10-20 minute window lost about 0.05R less per trade with about half the trades; 30 minutes was worse; not significant; still negative after costs.

MNQ/MES 1-minute research (README claim; about 3.7 years Dukascopy, about 420 NY sessions per market): ORB, noise-boundary momentum, first-half-hour momentum, ICT sweep reversals, and linear/GBM walk-forward models were none reliably profitable after costs. Costs drive the losses (-0.08R NQ, -0.17R S&P per trade); overnight and tight-stop signals lose 3-5x more. Filters cut NQ from 20,031 trades (-1,655R) to 2,460 (-75R).

Target Win Rate controller (README claim; 12 markets): targets 85/90/95% realised 84.9/89.6/93.7%. The controller works, but the average trade was about 0R before costs; a high win % from tiny targets is not an edge.

The later study independently replicates every early-engine conclusion. Pools beyond distance: +0.1 +/- 0.4 pp (1H, n 52,762). No reversal edge after sweeps: REJECT +1.5 +/- 0.7 pp continuation at 1H. D called the first side right 47.4-52.7% on 8 markets. FVG and OB reach equal to a distance-matched random level. The engine's FVG quality is not a target signal (rejected FVGs +7.0 pp, z 3.3, CME 1H). Breakers are weak targets (-4.9 to -8.3 pp at 1H). iFVG retest holds 49-50% (n about 25,000). Opposing FVGs in the path cut reach by 2-3 pp, the one supported ICT path claim. The intraday volatility clock is real (hour bias up to 17 pp).

LFP simulator (re-run by me): 15/15 behavioural checks pass. On driftless random walks the side-share reading flips about every 68 bars and is EXTREME on 7.35% of bars, which shows the share is not evidence of direction. LFP was never tested on real-data outcomes.

Net lesson for APEX: geometry (distance, volatility, clock) is the backbone. ICT labels, sweep reversals and fixed bias votes failed every test. Costs dominate short-horizon futures signals. Ungated learners over-fit. Keep features neutral and measure them per chart behind prequential gates, and default to neutral when evidence is weak.

result.summary:
I inspected three legacy projects: XAUUSD Fast/Balanced Pro (a Pine v6 strategy), buy_sell_indicator (Pine v5) and MNQ 5m ORB (indicator, strategy, Python backtest and PineTS harness). Each legacy copy is byte-identical to its origin commit. The copy leaves out package.json, which pins pinets 0.10.0 and pinescript-v6-validator 0.4.3; I read it from the origin branch.

What I ran this session:
- Data: the public NQ/MNQ dataset, fetched exactly as fetch_data.sh does (repo HEAD 0ee4392, SHA-256 recorded). The NQ 1m file is exactly 1,048,576 lines, Excel's row limit, and ends 2025-12-11.
- T1 backtest: the unmodified prepare_data.py and backtest.py reproduced every README number exactly (729 trades, 85.7% win, PF 1.24, +$4,548, cost stress, neighbour grid, 2026 rows).
- T2 harness: the unmodified PineTS verify.py, with the pinned versions, printed ALL CHECKS PASSED. Strategy net was $832 / $1,975 / $2,004.50.
- T3 static validator on all four scripts.
- T4 my own baseline analysis:
  - Mechanical win rate at 0.2R is 83.3%, against 85.7% observed and an 84.6% cost-adjusted break-even.
  - Random direction on the same bars and geometry (2,000 draws) gives a median win of 83.3% and a median PF of 0.98. The rule beat 99.55% of those draws in-sample.
  - Bootstrap 95% CI for mean P&L per trade: -$0.52 to +$12.60 (t = 1.87). PF CI: 0.98 to 1.59.
- T5 buy/sell vote counts on NQ 1H and 4H, 2023-2025: min_signals = 3 fired 0 times.
- T6 PineTS smoke run of XAUUSD: it ran, although TradingView would reject the script, and its VWAP equalled hlc3 on every bar.

FAST vs BALANCED in project A are pure threshold presets on one engine:

| Setting | FAST | BALANCED |
|---|---|---|
| Minimum score | 42 | 58 |
| Minimum alignment | 1 | 2 |
| Same-direction cooldown (bars) | 3 | 6 |
| Bars since any signal | 2 | 4 |
| Chop veto at | 85 | 68 |
| Chase veto at | 85 | 62 |
| Extreme-volatility veto | off | on |

None of these thresholds was ever tested.

Project A does not compile: f_killLines (lines 731-746) reassigns globals inside a function, which the v6 docs say is a compile error. It also has v6 lazy-evaluation corruption of ta.crossover, a VWAP that never resets, and an HTF timing mismatch between historical and realtime bars.

Project C is the only project with real evidence, and it is weak:
- Its high win rate is a product of the 0.2R/1R geometry.
- Its holdout was spent when the target was retuned from 0.5R to 0.2R after the 2026 data had been seen.
- The 2026 MNQ file has PF 0.74.
- Its rejected-idea results and its bootstrap are claims only: those scripts were never committed.

The harness proves agreement between two implementations by the same author, not that TradingView compiles the script or that runtimes agree on every construct. The report sets out its exact mechanics and a layered template (L0-L8) for APEX validation.
preserve: Confirm-on-close signal gate, next-bar-open fills and a written non-repaint statement (XAUUSD lines 32-48, 86, 681; ORB indicator lines 152 and 201)
ATR-normalised thresholds throughout project A (instrument-agnostic, spec §13.1)
Project A's debug 'blocked by' table (lines 1162-1248), kept as a concept for APEX reason codes and the debug dashboard, OFF by default

The Python broker-emulator semantics in bt.simulate (bt.py 76-140): decide on the close, fill at the next open, SL/TP from the fill, stop first on same-bar ambiguity, gaps fill at the open, EOD exit. It reproduced exactly; use it as the APEX offline evaluator core.
TV-equivalent reference helpers in bt.py (ema/rma/rsi/atr/dmi, and htf_ema emulating [1] + lookahead_on) as the offline parity library
The backtest protocol (design 2023-24 / validation 2025 / holdout, neighbour grid, per-year and monthly tables, cost stress), extended with baselines and confidence intervals
The ORB status-line UX ('Watching for breakout', 'Done for today'), kept as a concept for a minimal panel
rework: FAST/BALANCED (XAUUSD 131-159, 654-694): keep the user's model of one engine with two presets. BALANCED should demand a higher bias threshold, more de-correlated evidence groups, persistence and wider spacing. Add STRONG states. Fix the dual-use iAlExmpt input and the mislabelled 'opposite' spacing. Never attach win rates or probabilities to a mode.
Momentum composite that averages RSI, MACD and DMI (212-218): keep the redundancy principle, but rebuild it as one documented normalised momentum feature
Chop and chase scores (382-410): rebuild them as percentile-based regime and location measures with hysteresis (spec §9 and §16)
Manual confirmed pivots with consumed BOS/CHoCH levels (267-314): the logic is sound, but the DOL v2 structure engine supersedes it. Remove the ta.* calls placed inside and/or.
Dashboard of strategy stats: an indicator cannot read strategy.*. Replace it with a ledger that shows the geometry-matched baseline and break-even beside every win rate.

final_ref.liquidity_levels (PDH/PDL/ONH/ONL as known at the bar close, verified on every bar): generalise it away from the NY/CME constants and the 0.25 tick, and decide whether 'swept' should include the current bar

PineTS equivalence harness: keep the method (debug plots appended to the unmodified source, a Python reference, per-bar equality). Add custom lints (global reassignment in functions, ta.* in and/or, HTF pattern), a runtime-parity register, start-point invariance, stream/update repaint tests and asserted strategy metrics. Pin versions and record data hashes.
Opening range: keep it only as a liquidity source (OR high/low pools) and as a volatility unit, not as a signal
The ORB on-chart stats table: keep the honest labelling (in-sample, per contract, after cost), and add the break-even win rate and a baseline
drop: XAUUSD 10-engine OR trigger set (450-479): a forced-signal design, and five of the engines (pullback, VWAP reclaim, breakout, sweep reversal, compression expansion) are contested by the user's own NQ tests or by the study
XAUUSD additive point score (515-634): it counts correlated trend features as independent, has no calibration and has no data-quality weights
XAUUSD 3-target partial-exit trade manager and risk sizing (768-1057): APEX is an indicator, exits cannot create expectancy, and the fractional quantities are CFD-specific
XAUUSD session VWAP (245-259): the reset is broken on a '0000-0000' session
XAUUSD HTF block (360-371): expr[1] with lookahead_off is superseded by the [1] + lookahead_on pattern

The whole buy_sell_indicator: it is v5, fails to compile (label.style_label_lower), its show_rsi toggle hides every signal, two inputs are dead, its RSI-state-plus-cross vote is contradictory (3-of-3 never fires), and it uses background fills and untested marketing claims
The ORB signal rule as an APEX signal: hardcoded to MNQ/NQ, 5m and NY sessions, with weak and contested evidence and a spent holdout
The ORB sweep-first filter and LIQ tag as a signal booster: better in-sample (PF 1.62 on 290 trades), but it failed on 2026 (PF 0.83 on 23 trades and 0.51 on 18)
defects: BLOCKER XAUUSD 731-746: f_killLines assigns lnEnt := na (and the other line variables) to globals inside a function. The v6 manual says user-defined functions 'cannot modify' globals and that this causes a compilation error. Neither the validator nor PineTS caught it.

HIGH XAUUSD 458-459, 475-476 (also 297-298): v6 evaluates and/or lazily, so ta.crossover/ta.crossunder only run on some bars and their history is corrupted. Engine J's cross runs only while compActive is true; engine I's second and third crosses run only when the earlier ones are false.

HIGH XAUUSD 99 and 245: a '0000-0000' VWAP session is a 7-day, 24-hour session, so newVwapSes never fires after the first bar and the VWAP never resets, despite the 'calendar day' tooltip. This is reasoned from the docs. PineTS instead returned VWAP = hlc3 on every bar.
MEDIUM XAUUSD 345-346 and 395-396: ta.highest and ta.lowest are called inside if blocks and ternaries, so their history has gaps (validator S2 warnings)

MEDIUM XAUUSD 360-364: request.security(expr[1], lookahead_off) takes a new historical value at the end of each HTF period, but realtime takes the developing bar's value, so historical and realtime timing differ
MEDIUM XAUUSD 801-856: 'AVG R (model)' is optimistic. When TP1 and SL hit in the same bar, TP1 is credited and the remainder is booked at the new break-even stop.
LOW XAUUSD 665-668: cooldown counters increment on barstate.isnew, which the docs say differs between historical and realtime bars (its behaviour in a close-only strategy is unverified)

LOW XAUUSD 136 and 690-694: one input serves as both the alignment exemption and the extreme-volatility threshold. Lines 141-142 and 898: the 'opposite signals' spacing actually uses barsSinceAny. Lines 909-939: signals depend on trade state and equity. Line 862: lines are finalised for the wrong trade when iMaxTrades > 1. Array tSL0 is dead (701, 871, 1003). Buy and sell code is duplicated as mirrors.

buy_sell_indicator line 116: label.style_label_lower does not exist (validator error, absent from the docs). Lines 81 and 85: show_rsi gates every signal. Lines 28-29: show_ma and show_macd are dead. Lines 113-117: a label is added every realtime bar. There is no confirmation gate, so alertcondition fires intrabar.

MNQ ORB: hardcoded syminfo.root MNQ/NQ, 5m and the 09:30/16:00/18:00 NY constants (plus a 0.25 tick in Python). Early-close holidays are not handled. sslSwept/bslSwept include the signal bar, contradicting the README's 'earlier that morning'. The strategy's canSignal has no barstate.isconfirmed guard if a user enables every-tick recalculation.

MNQ ORB research: the rejected-idea scripts and the 0.5R-era bootstrap were never committed (claims only). verify.py's paths assume the original layout, so it does not run from the flattened legacy copy. package.json is missing from the copy. Strategy wins and net are printed but never asserted. Per-year slicing causes boundary effects: 90 vs 91 sweep-ON trades in 2025.
userPreferences: Wants modes named exactly FAST and BALANCED: FAST is responsive with more signals, BALANCED requires more score and agreement with fewer signals
Wants clear BUY/SELL markers: triangles or labelup/labeldown, buy green (#00c853/#00e676 or #089981) and sell red (#ff3d00 or #f23645)
Wants Entry, SL and TP levels on signal labels and in alert messages, plus an alert when a trade closes
Wants a grade (A+/A/B/C), a regime readout and a compact dark dashboard: #101418/#1b2027 cells, cyan #00e5ff header, small text
Wants honest, real statistics only ('nothing is fabricated'): per-year tables, cost stress, an explicit 'not a blind test any more', and plain-language risk boxes ('Read this first')
Values a high win rate: the ORB target was retuned from 0.5R to 0.2R for about 86%. APEX must educate with WIN vs break-even rather than chase this.
Wants a debug 'why didn't it fire' view, and confirmed-bar non-repainting by default with a written statement
Treats HTF as supporting evidence, not a veto, by default (strict HTF off)
Wants liquidity levels (PDH/PDL, ONH/ONL) that fade once swept, with × markers and a check mark in the table
Asks for scripts to be verified several independent ways because no TradingView compiler is available offline, and asks to be sent the exact error and line if TradingView rejects one
Writes informally and is not a programmer: READMEs are plain-language, with install steps and tables
lessonsFromTesting: The ORB win rate is set by geometry: at 0.2R a driftless random walk wins 83.3%, against 85.7% observed and an 84.6% cost-adjusted break-even (729 trades, NQ 5m 2023-2025, I ran this). Always report WIN minus break-even, or realised R, never a bare win rate. This agrees with trade_mgmt §1.2.

ORB breakout direction carries a little in-sample information: it beat 99.55% of 2,000 random-direction draws with the same geometry (random median PF 0.98). The bootstrap 95% CI for mean P&L per trade is -$0.52 to +$12.60 (t = 1.87), and the 2026 MNQ file has PF 0.74 on 41 trades. Class C, weak. The study's Mesfin 2026 result (947 MNQ days, ORB long T 1.17-1.50) agrees.

Retuning after a blind test destroys it: the 0.5R rule lost on both 2026 files (-$224 NQ on 50 trades, -$1,674 MNQ on 41), then 0.2R was chosen after seeing them. APEX needs a pre-registered holdout that is never retuned.

The selected ORB cell (15-minute range, 0.8 strength) is the best 0.2R cell of the design grid, and five of its eight neighbours have PF below 1 in at least one period. Selection at the edge of a fragile grid means overfitting risk.
Costs dominate small targets: PF falls from 1.24 to 1.16 to 1.08 as round-trip cost rises from 1.5 to 2.5 to 3.5 points (729 trades, I ran this)

The liquidity-sweep-first filter improved in-sample (PF 1.24 to 1.62, 729 to 290 trades, 2023-25) but failed out of sample (PF 0.83 on 23 NQ trades and 0.51 on 18 MNQ trades in 2026). This is reproduced.

Rejected by the user's NQ 5m tests (claims only, scripts not committed): sweep-fade reversals; EMA 9/21/50 pullback + VWAP (PF about 0.9); RSI(2) mean reversion (about 65% win, PF 0.87-0.97); a 30-minute OR; HTF, VWAP, ADX, volume, gap and OR-size filters; extra trades per day; limit retest entries; profit-lock stops
Targets below 0.2R reach 88-92% win rates but fail on 2026 data (0.1R: PF 1.14 in-sample, 0.58 on 2026 NQ). This is reproduced.
Voting that ANDs a persistent state with one-bar events creates dead modes: buy_sell 3-of-3 fired 0 times in 3 years on NQ 1H and 4H, and RSI+MA never co-occurred (I ran this)

The PineTS harness gave exact per-bar parity for ORB (signals, trades, levels and sweep flags across 3 years with the filter on and off) but has blind spots. It executed XAUUSD although TradingView would reject the script, and it diverged on a session VWAP (hlc3 on every bar). It does not test realtime, rollback, request.security or start-point invariance, and it only prints strategy fills. Parity holds per construct, and PineTS is not a compiler.

The static validator (0.4.3) caught the unknown label constant and if/ternary ta.* gaps, but missed reassignment of globals inside functions and ta.* calls inside lazy and/or. APEX needs custom lints for both.
